findings.reason: without an ownership/identity guard the repair kills unrelated processes, so the section must state what qualifies a pid to be ended before it can be implemented safely.
findings.text: §2 makes `signal_worker` kill every process whose cwd or open fd resolves under the run's worktree via `_processes_holding`, but that enumerator has no ownership or identity attribution (it returns any pid holding the path, including a peer session or a coordinator that cd'd in) and its cited contract is "never killed", so a node implementing §2 literally builds an over-broad kill path — the `kill -1`-class hazard `signal_worker`'s docstring exists to prevent — while the plan asserts the extension is safe by pointing at those very enumerators

findings.reason: the true blast radius is smaller than claimed, which does not alter the decision to extend the one signal owner.
findings.text: §2 states "Nine modules import it" of `signal_worker`, but only four production modules import it (`dispatch_launch`, `standing_suite`, etc., excluding the definition site in `routing.py`; test modules account for the rest)

findings.reason: the dependency the roadmap reads does not carry it, so a dispatch of §2 will be scheduled without serialization and two writers will collide on `routing.py`.
findings.text: §2 serializes on the live run `a-worktree-release-is-whole` because that run also writes `reckon/crew/routing.py` (confirmed: its pointer's `write_paths` includes that file and it belongs to a different plan, crew-runtime-positive-controls §47), yet the dependency appears only in §2 prose; `plan-section-depends-on` declares only `s3→s2`, and `plan-standalone` states the plan waits on none

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited file, symbol and test resolves (`signal_worker`, `_processes_holding`, `_process_children`/`_live_descendant`, `local_liveness`, `resume_plan`, `_launcher_refusal`, `_observed_end_refusal`, `terminate`, and all six named test files exist); the run id `a-worktree-release-is-whole` resolves to a live pointer, and the `#s2` depends-on target is a real section.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — both nodes name a declared negative control that can fail (§2 "signals the supervisor pid alone, fails the first case"; §3 "restores the cause the reproduction named, fails the reproduced case").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — negative controls are "logged under the run directory", a durable path under the operator's crew state, not a scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — new symbols and the new test file are named by mechanism (`test_a_worker_never_outlives_its_supervisor.py`); no plan labels, ticket numbers or changelog prose reach the code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2's mechanism extends `signal_worker` to end "the processes holding the run's worktree as their working directory, through the existing enumerators", but `_processes_holding` is documented report-only ("A holder is only ever reported, never killed") and `signal_worker`'s own docstring states its invariant is that "ending one worker is never worth the risk of ending everything"; the plan reverses both cited contracts without naming what makes a holder safe to kill.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable (a worker never outlives its supervisor, incl. its classification) and §3 one (a resume never launches beside a live attempt); each closes on a single test verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §2 declares in prose that it waits for the external run `a-worktree-release-is-whole` (crew-runtime-positive-controls §47) to merge before writing `reckon/crew/routing.py`, but `plan-section-depends-on` carries only `s3→s2` and `plan-standalone` asserts the plan "wait[s] on none".
